Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The blood-first workflow identified 12.7% as ineligible at the biomarker stage, but the poster does not establish how many scans it saved. For trial planning, quantify downstream utilization and false exclusions before generalizing this sequence.

Study design

Descriptive analysis of the prescreening flow of START (NCT05531656), which applied blood biomarkers before MRI and amyloid confirmation.

Key quantitative results

  • 1,646 were screened overall; among 1,617 evaluable participants, 206 (12.7%) were flagged ineligible by plasma biomarkers before MRI and PET or CSF confirmation.
  • 610 reached confirmation and 545 were randomized. The report did not estimate counterfactual scans avoided or missed amyloid-positive participants.

What changed

1,646 were screened overall; among 1,617 evaluable participants, 206 (12.7%) were flagged ineligible by plasma biomarkers before MRI and PET or CSF confirmation.

Strength of evidence

Conference trial-screening workflow analysis. Key constraints: no comparative workflow.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

For trial planning, quantify downstream utilization and false exclusions before generalizing this sequence.

Field medical relevance

Interpret alongside these constraints: Reasons for ineligibility could overlap; No demonstrated clinical-care cutoff or missed-positive rate.

Quanterix or platform relevance

For trial planning, quantify downstream utilization and false exclusions before generalizing this sequence.

Access or reimbursement relevance

These results do not by themselves establish routine availability or payer coverage.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Were 206 scans demonstrably avoided?
No. The poster reports flow and possible ineligibility, not a comparison showing actual scan savings.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • No comparative workflow
  • Reasons for ineligibility could overlap
  • No demonstrated clinical-care cutoff or missed-positive rate
